title: Aloo Methi
subtitle: Potatoes and dried fenugreek leaves cooked with whole spices
excerpt: Diced potato cooked dry with fenugreek leaves and a light spice base. The fenugreek gives a pleasantly bitter edge. Fast, cheap, and good with flatbreads or rice.
sourceNotes: North Indian home cooking. A simple dry vegetable dish common across Punjab and Uttar Pradesh.

recipe.batchNotes: Use a large, wide frying pan so the potatoes cook dry rather than steam.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps well in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat in a pan with a small splash of water.

content.text: Aloo methi is a dry potato dish with a gentle bitter note from the fenugreek leaves. Keep the lid off once the spice base is set so the potatoes stay firm rather than going to mush.

items.prepNote: peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

content.text: Heat the oil in the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and fry for 20 seconds until they pop and smell toasted.
Add the onion and cook for 7 minutes, stirring often, until soft and pale gold.
Add the garlic and ginger. Stir for 1 minute. Add the turmeric, coriander, chilli powder, and salt. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add the potato cubes and stir well to coat in the spice base. Add 4 tablespoons of water and stir again.
Cover the pan with a lid. Cook on a medium-low heat for 12 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until the potato is just tender.
Remove the lid. Crumble in the fenugreek leaves and stir through. Cook uncovered for 3 minutes to drive off any remaining moisture.
Stir in the garam masala. Taste and adjust salt. Squeeze over lemon juice if using and serve immediately.

items.symptom: The potatoes are sticking to the pan.
items.cause: The heat is too high or there is not enough oil.
items.fix: Add a tablespoon of water and stir immediately to release any stuck pieces. Lower the heat.

items.symptom: The fenugreek taste is very bitter.
items.cause: Too much dried leaf was used, or the leaves were not crushed.
items.fix: Crush the leaves between your palms before adding. Use 2 tablespoons rather than 3 next time.

items.symptom: The potatoes are still hard after 12 minutes.
items.cause: The cubes were too large or the heat too low.
items.fix: Add 2 tablespoons of water, cover again, and cook for a further 5 minutes on a medium heat.
